evidence: packages/types/Calendar.d.ts:221 changes the interface to createEvent(event, credentialId: number). The implementations that leave out the second parameter (office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:72, larkcalendar:125, packages/lib/CalendarService.ts:125, exchange*, CRM apps) still type-check, because TypeScript lets an implementing method take fewer parameters than the interface (parameter bivariance/arity rule). Only Google (googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:87) uses credentialId, and it declares it. CalendarManager.ts passes credential.id to every implementation, and the ones that don't need it ignore it. There is no compile or runtime error.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:758-761 turns every PrismaClientKnownRequestError into a 400, including server-side failures such as DB constraint or timeout codes. Those are not client errors, so the claim is accurate. It is low impact, though: the only Prisma call in loadUsers is a simple user.findMany (line ~731), and connection failures throw PrismaClientInitializationError or UnknownRequestError, which go to the 500 branch. The HttpError check is also dead because nothing inside the try throws HttpError.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:337-373: inside `for (const destination of event.destinationCalendar)`, every credential missing from this.calendarCredentials (i.e. any co-host's credential) triggers its own awaited prisma.credential.findUnique at line 344. So there is one query per extra host. This is technically a sequential per-item query, but the number of hosts on a collective event is small, and each iteration also awaits an external calendar API call in createEvent, which costs far more than the query. Batching with findMany is a nice-to-have, not a real performance problem.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:117-118: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []; if (evt.location === MeetLocationType && mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar")` has no optional chaining. handleNewBooking.ts:1063-1067 sets destinationCalendar to null when neither the event type nor the organizer has one, so mainHostDestinationCalendar is undefined. If the booking location is Google Meet, that throws a TypeError. This is the exact scenario the fallback is meant to handle ('Google Meet is selected w/o a Google Cal'). Other call sites (googlecalendar CalendarService.ts:122, lib/CalendarService.ts:163) correctly use `?.`. Fix: `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:315-317 (deleteEvent): `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. The find only runs when externalCalendarId is falsy, so it compares against null/undefined and effectively never matches. The fallback is dead code. The old code fell back to destinationCalendar.externalId; now deletes for references without externalCalendarId (legacy bookings) always go to 'primary' and can miss events created on a non-primary selected calendar. The fallback should pick the destination calendar that matches this credential (e.g. by credentialId), or the first one.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:254-256 (updateEvent) has the same dead-code pattern: the find runs only when externalCalendarId is falsy and compares cal.externalId to that falsy value, so it returns undefined. selectedCalendar then reaches calendar.events.update as calendarId: undefined (line 261) with no 'primary' default. Updates/reschedules of references that lack externalCalendarId therefore fail against the Google API, where before this PR they used destinationCalendar.externalId. This is a regression.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:344-367 (createAllCalendarEvents) and :517-540 (updateAllCalendarEvents) contain the same ~25-line block: prisma.credential.findUnique with include app.slug, then mapping to CredentialWithAppName. A third, slightly different copy is at EventManager.ts:557 and handleCancelBooking.ts:433. Extracting a private getCredentialById helper would remove the duplication and also make batching (issues 2/10) easier. It is maintainability only, with no behavior impact.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1078 uses `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`. The optional chaining means a null destinationCalendar can never throw, so the runtime-error claim is wrong. There is a related real gap: when the organizer/event type has no destination calendar (line 1063-1067 yields null), the co-hosts' teamDestinationCalendars are silently dropped, and co-hosts don't get calendar events, which defeats the purpose of the PR. Simply initializing to [] is not a full fix, though: createAllCalendarEvents (EventManager.ts:337) would then skip the organizer's default-credential fallback branch.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/organizations/create.handler.ts:151 changes `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`, which inverts the condition. Before, the slug was set directly only when billing was disabled; with billing on it was stored only as metadata.requestedSlug until payment. Now the slug is set directly when billing is enabled (so the payment gate is bypassed), and self-hosted/no-billing instances get no slug. Line 153 (requestedSlug) is semantically unchanged. This change is unrelated to the destinationCalendar work and should be reverted to `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED`.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:724-762: the plain Error('dynamicUserList is not properly defined or empty.') thrown at line 728 (and 'eventType.hosts is not properly defined.') is not an HttpError or Prisma error, so the catch at 761 replaces it with a generic 500 'Unable to load users'. The specific message is lost, and a client-input problem is reported as a server error. Throwing HttpError({statusCode: 400, ...}) directly at those points would keep the message. Separately, this refactor also drops the `organization: { select: { slug } }` select from the dynamic-user query that was there before the PR. That is unrelated scope creep worth flagging.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:502-551: `for (const reference of calendarReference)` awaits prisma.credential.findUnique (line 517) for each reference whose credential isn't in this.calendarCredentials. This is the same sequential per-reference pattern as issue 2. The number of references is bounded by the number of hosts (small), and each one also triggers an external updateEvent call, so the impact is minor. It could be batched together with the issue-6 helper.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:423-440: for each _calendar reference whose credentialId isn't in bookingToDelete.user.credentials, an awaited prisma.credential.findUnique runs (line 433). This is accurate, but the number of references equals the number of collective hosts (small), and each one is followed by an external deleteEvent call, so the extra queries are negligible. Batching is an optional optimization.
